<<The Airline's Shift>>

Section 1 The financial report landed on the desk like a heavy stone. EasyJet saw its profits fall 17% last year. The shadow of the control tower loomed over the decision-making process. Carolyn McCall knew the aviation society was watching closely. More than £100m lost due to the slump in the pound after the Brexit vote. Revenues exceeded £5bn, yet the currency weakness brought additional costs.

Section 2 They reported a record year for passenger numbers, flying 80.2 million people. But while revenues grew, fares dipped to fill seats. They did not dare to ignore the difficult year for the industry. Stelios Haji-Ioannou held a third of shares. There was no fishing for excuses regarding the EU ownership rules. The airline would ask for new powers to force UK shareholders to sell up if necessary.

Section 3 Shares rose by more than 5% in early trading. High levels of forward bookings signaled confidence. McCall said the move was a technical thing and they had no concerns. They would treat the situation with administrative precision. The revenue improvement was primarily as a result of some capacity leaving the market. The strategic advantage remained intact despite the bankruptcies elsewhere.
